forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Mansfield's medium-term plan shows General Fund deficits of £1.594m in 2027/28, rising to £4.372m by 2029/30
news_drafts.lead:
Mansfield District Council's Cabinet considered a medium term financial plan for 2027/28 to 2029/30 that shows a deficit on the General Fund revenue budget in each of its three years. The deficit is £1.594m in 2027/28, £3.366m in 2028/29 and £4.372m in 2029/30. The General Fund is the account that pays for council services other than council housing.

The paper attributes the 2027/28 deficit mainly to the 2026/27 reset of business rates, which removed local growth from the base the council retains. Appendix 1 shows the deficit widening in every year of the plan. The paper says: "There is an on-going deficit over the medium term at a time where public sector funding becomes tighter."

The council's section 151 officer, its chief finance officer, states that the council needs to be prepared to make decisions on the services it provides, the level at which they are provided and how they are delivered. The paper records the head of paid service, the council's chief executive, as saying savings must be more than just financially driven.
news_drafts.paper_title: Cabinet Report - Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/28 to 2029/30

news_drafts.headline: Mansfield Council carries forward £33.8m of capital investment to next year as major projects slip.
news_drafts.lead: Mansfield Council is deferring £33.8 million of planned capital spending from 2026/27 to 2027/28, with only 66 per cent of its General Fund capital programme forecast to be delivered this year. The carry-forwards — £26.8 million from the General Fund and £7 million from the Housing Revenue Account, which funds the council's own housing stock — reflect delays across major projects including the Mansfield Connect digital transformation programme, which is forecast to spend only £1 million of a £23.7 million budget, and the White Hart Street housing development, which is expected to deliver only £2.3 million of its £9.3 million allocation. The council's revenue budget, however, is broadly on track, with a £169,000 surplus forecast for the year. Interest income is running £300,000 ahead of budget due to higher-than-expected rates, offsetting pressures from higher-than-budgeted vacancies in housing stock and unmet savings targets across 15 service areas.

news_drafts.headline: Mansfield Council borrows £15m in quarter with half its debt due within a year
news_drafts.lead: Mansfield Council borrowed £15m in the first three months of 2026/27 and expects to raise £50m more this year, taking total debt toward £135m. Nearly half its existing borrowing—£46.8m of £98.8m—matures within 12 months, forcing the council to refinance at short notice. The council is betting that interest rates will fall to limit refinancing costs, but early repayment charges on its £52.7m Public Works Loan Board debt are so expensive that it cannot reschedule loans if rates hold steady or rise. Treasury management papers show investment income is running £300,000 above budget because base rates remained at 3.75% longer than forecast, but this benefit is temporary and will reverse if rates fall as expected.

findings.paper_title: Cabinet Report - Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/28 to 2029/30
findings.headline: The 2027/28 capital programme includes £8,000k for Mansfield Connect, rising to £16,687k in 2028/29.
findings.detail: The paper lists Mansfield Connect alongside fleet and food waste vehicle acquisition and Pride in Place funded works. The General Fund capital programme totals £16,011k in 2027/28 and £21,627k in 2028/29.
findings.matters: A large single scheme in the General Fund capital programme is a concentration of spend that finance officers and lenders will follow through delivery.
findings.quote: The proposed three-year programme includes works on Mansfield Connect

findings.paper_title: Cabinet Report - Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/28 to 2029/30
findings.headline: Local elections for Mansfield District Council will go ahead in May 2027 on existing boundaries, after the government paused local government reorganisation.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the LGR decision on the Nottinghamshire footprint has been withdrawn, with a new decision expected by early 2027. The S151 Officer says it is prudent to budget beyond 2028/29 as a result.
findings.matters: A pause in reorganisation changes when the budget will be handed over, which affects lenders and finance officers planning for an authority transition.
findings.quote: Local elections, including those for Mansfield District Council, will now go ahead in May 2027 based on existing council boundaries.

findings.paper_title: Cabinet Report - Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/28 to 2029/30
findings.headline: General Fund interest payable is budgeted at £2,658k for 2027/28 and £3,167k for 2029/30, while MRP rises from £952k to £2,408k.
findings.detail: The rise in interest payable and MRP reflects the borrowing in the capital programme. The paper's figures for interest receivable stay at £641k in each year.
findings.matters: Rising debt costs and MRP charges reduce the revenue headroom available for services, and this is an increase peer councils with new capital programmes will also see.

findings.paper_title: Cabinet Report - Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/28 to 2029/30
findings.headline: Investment property income is budgeted at £2,837k in 2027/28 and the council says a high proportion of its income comes from commercial and industrial rents.
findings.detail: The paper states that businesses face the same energy and staffing pressures as the council, and that the council needs to monitor this income stream closely.
findings.matters: Commercial rental income is a large income line for councils with property portfolios, and lenders assess its exposure to tenant pressures.
findings.quote: The Council generates a high proportion of its income from commercial/industrial rents.

findings.paper_title: Cabinet Report - Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/28 to 2029/30
findings.headline: The budget includes £1,100m as the council's share of Extended Producer Responsibility grant in 2026/27, with no provision made for the 2027/28 amount.
findings.detail: The paper says the 2027/28 amount has not yet been announced and that no provision has been made in the budget for this grant or related expenditure.
findings.matters: A grant received in one year but not yet confirmed for the next is an income gap that peer councils on the same scheme will need to plan for.
findings.quote: No provision has been made in the budget for this grant or related expenditure.
